recommendations.text: Implement exportCsv(contacts) in src/export/csv.js, returning CSV file content as a string.
Include a header row with columns name,email,phone in that order, followed by one row per contact in input order. Represent missing values as empty fields.

Read docs/CONVENTIONS.md and the existing export implementations and tests to establish module exports, CSV formatting, line endings, trailing newline behavior, contact representation, and missing-value semantics. Follow the project's applicable conventions.
Ensure values containing commas, double quotes, or line breaks remain single CSV fields through appropriate quoting and escaping, consistent with project conventions.

Add tests covering the exact header and column order, multiple contacts, missing values, empty input producing the header without contact rows, and CSV quoting and escaping. Assert exact string output according to the established conventions.
Run the project's test suite using npm test, verifying the command against the repository and confirming that new and existing tests pass.
Keep this change focused on string-based CSV export and tests; do not add file writing, download UI, CSV import, or address-book schema changes.

spec.rawIntent: Add a CSV export of the address book: `exportCsv(contacts)` in src/export/csv.js returns the file content as a string with the columns name, email and phone, in that order, with a header row. A missing value is an empty field. Follow the export conventions of this project (docs/CONVENTIONS.md). Include tests.
